domain: Constitutional Law / Political Transitions / Post-Revolutionary State-Building
topic_summary: Analysis of competing interpretations of Bangladesh's July 2024 National Charter following the mass uprising that ousted Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina. The charter emerged from student-led protests and interim government formation, creating a foundational document whose interpretation determines sovereign legitimacy, institutional authority, and the boundaries of political contestation in post-Awami League Bangladesh.

key_entities: Student Coordination Movement (primary revolutionary actor; charter drafters)
Interim Government led by Muhammad Yunus (transitional authority)
Military/Security Apparatus (institutional continuity actor; interpretive authority contested)
key_tensions: Secular democratic institutionalism vs religiously-guided nationalism (charter interpretation axis)
Revolutionary legitimacy vs constitutional continuity (sovereign authority grounding)
Student movement autonomy vs military institutional control (interpretive authority structure)

commitment_system_recognition.kernel_description: The July 2024 National Charter as stabilized commitment establishing post-revolutionary sovereign legitimacy and institutional authority boundaries
commitment_system_recognition.authority_description: Contested between student movement (revolutionary mandate), interim government (administrative custody), military (institutional continuity), and political parties (electoral legitimacy claims)

readings.commitment: Charter mandates secular democratic institutions with military subordination to civilian authority
readings.authority_grounding: Student movement revolutionary mandate plus constitutional reform tradition (1972 baseline)
readings.expected_structural_delta: Political Islam actors excluded or constrained; military as subordinate institution; victim set includes Jamaat-e-Islami and military autonomous authority

readings.commitment: Charter establishes Islamic-nationalist framework with religious identity as sovereign legitimacy ground
readings.authority_grounding: Mass uprising interpreted as rejection of secular Awami League; Islamic parties' participation legitimizes religious grounding
readings.expected_structural_delta: Secular institutions constrained; religious law or norms gain constitutional status; victim set includes secular civil society and religious minorities

readings.commitment: Charter ratifies military as permanent institutional guardian ensuring stability
readings.authority_grounding: Military institutional continuity across regime transitions; self-claimed role as national unity guarantor
readings.expected_structural_delta: Civilian institutions subordinated to military veto authority; political contestation bounded by security apparatus; victim set includes autonomous political parties and student movement

axiom_contradictions.basis: No single coherent framework can simultaneously hold that religious identity is constitutionally irrelevant to sovereign legitimacy (secular baseline) and that religious identity grounds sovereign legitimacy (Islamic framework). Accepting one axiom as true requires rejecting the other as false.

No single coherent framework can simultaneously hold that civilian authority is supreme and final (democratic constitutionalism) and that military institutional authority overrides civilian decisions (custodian model). The axioms are mutually exclusive regarding ultimate sovereign location.

These axioms can coexist in a hybrid framework (military guaranteeing Islamic order). This pair does NOT meet the mutual exclusivity test and is therefore NOT declared contradictory despite different institutional priorities.

axes.human_readable: Secular Democratic Reading (Charter as Civilian Supremacy Mandate)
axes.structural_delta: Charter interpreted as mandate for secular institutions with military subordination and political Islam constraints
axes.primary_observable: Interim government policy on Jamaat-e-Islami participation; military budget autonomy vs civilian oversight; constitutional reform proposals on secularism clauses
axes.selection_reason: Highest structural distinctiveness; represents revolutionary movement's stated interpretation; clearest victim set (Jamaat + military autonomous authority)

axes.human_readable: Guided Nationalism Reading (Charter as Islamic Framework Legitimation)
axes.structural_delta: Charter interpreted as establishing religious identity grounding for sovereign legitimacy with Islamic norms gaining constitutional status
axes.primary_observable: Constitutional reform proposals on state religion clauses; Jamaat-e-Islami electoral participation status; blasphemy law enforcement patterns
axes.selection_reason: Structurally opposite victim set from secular_democratic_reading; represents emergent coalition interpretation with BNP-Jamaat alignment

axes.human_readable: Military Custodian Reading (Charter as Institutional Guardian Ratification)
axes.structural_delta: Charter interpreted as ratifying military as permanent institutional authority ensuring national stability above civilian politics
axes.primary_observable: Military budget and command autonomy; frequency of security apparatus vetoes on civilian policy; student movement autonomy vs military control
axes.selection_reason: Third distinct reading with different beneficiary structure; captures institutional continuity axis orthogonal to secular/religious divide

axes.human_readable: Awami League Delegitimation (Charter as Permanent Exclusion Mechanism)
axes.structural_delta: Charter interpreted as establishing permanent exclusion of Awami League from political contestation
axes.primary_observable: Legal status of Awami League; eligibility rules for former AL members in elections; asset seizure scope
axes.selection_reason: Deferred: feeds into all three selected readings as upstream delegitimation mechanism; analytically important but structurally downstream-enabling rather than interpretation-defining

axes.human_readable: Student Movement Authority Eclipse (Revolutionary Mandate Decay)
axes.structural_delta: Student movement's revolutionary legitimacy claims erode as traditional power centers (military, parties) capture charter interpretation
axes.primary_observable: Student movement representation in interim government decisions; frequency of student veto on policy; media framing of movement authority
axes.selection_reason: Deferred: temporal decay mechanism rather than interpretive axis; relevant to military_custodian_reading emergence but lower structural priority than direct readings

deferred_axes.structural_delta: Charter as permanent exclusion mechanism for Awami League
deferred_axes.deferral_reason: Feeds into all three readings as upstream delegitimation mechanism; analytically critical but interpretation-enabling rather than interpretation-defining

deferred_axes.structural_delta: Revolutionary mandate decay as traditional power centers capture interpretation
deferred_axes.deferral_reason: Temporal decay mechanism; relevant to military reading emergence but lower structural distinctiveness than direct interpretive readings
